correctness.rationale: For each j>=2, n/p_j retains p_1, so its lambda value is at least p_1-1>p_j; hence n/p_j is stopping. Minimality gives d_min<=n/p_j, while squarefreeness and decreasing primes give d_min>=p_1...p_j>p_j^j. Therefore p_j^(j+1)<n. The quantifiers and j=t boundary are unchanged by the argument. Carmichael oddness supplies the strict gap p_1-1>p_j. The finite checker is explicitly non-probative for the infinite statement.

evidence: Shallue-Webster Theorem 2 gives p_(k+1)<(B/P_k)^(1/(d-k)) for the full ordered factorization of n.

value.rationale: The result turns a one-off cube-root fact used by a new exact compression representation into a structural depth hierarchy. It gives deterministic depth-specific prime universes, including substantially smaller cutoffs from depth three onward, without relying on empirical frequency data. This is a natural property of the representation rather than an arbitrary finite slice. No unmeasured compression gain is claimed.
